claim.statement: For a classical (Jacobi) bracket $P$ and the tethered bracket $P+\T$, the Jacobiator expands into nine terms. The three purely classical ones cancel by Jacobi of $P$, and the three purely tether terms vanish. So the Jacobiator equals the cyclic sum of the mixed terms, and Jacobi holds on a set $R$ iff that cyclic sum vanishes on $R$. It vanishes when $u$ is central for $P$, $P$ is homogeneous in its first slot, and $\Pi_u P(a,b)=0$.
claim.title: Nine-term Jacobi
